name: Hawthorn extract WS 1442 and cardiac arrhythmias
summary: In a single retrospective German database cohort of 4,550 WS 1442 users matched to 4,550 magnesium/potassium users, WS 1442 prescription was associated with a lower five-year incidence of atrial fibrillation/flutter, tachycardia, and other cardiac arrhythmias.
description: Wyss, Gündling & Kostev (Scientific Reports 2024) used the IQVIA Disease Analyzer database to compare 4,550 outpatients prescribed WS 1442 with 4,550 matched patients prescribed magnesium/potassium products (Tromcardin), followed for five years. Cox regression estimated adjusted hazard ratios for incident arrhythmias.
interpretation: This is a single non-randomized database study, not a trial: the comparison is against magnesium/potassium rather than placebo, and confounding by indication and unmeasured differences between the groups cannot be excluded despite adjustment. The reported associations are protective and consistent across three arrhythmia endpoints, but hazard ratios from one observational cohort are hypothesis-generating.
methodologyNotes: Adjusted hazard ratios (Cox regression) and 95% CIs are copied from the paper for each endpoint; the engine treats a hazard ratio as a risk-ratio approximation and flags it. Each study's ctrlRisk is the reported cumulative incidence in the magnesium/potassium group (atrial fibrillation/flutter 16.4%, tachycardia 9.4%, other arrhythmias 14.8%). Adjusted for obesity, diabetes, lipid disorders, hypertension, ischemic heart disease and other covariates per the paper.
